summary: Saturday policy check: YouTube's 1 Oct Shorts originality ranking targets re-uploaders, not us. Added two sourced topics (US debt per American, Zuckerberg's $1 salary vs $25.1M), rejected the stale petrol topic, and proposed fixing the 'illustrative numbers' line in descriptions.
why: The feed had 5 of 6 open topics in one format (how_they_make_money) and one blocked by stale facts; the new topics add money_scale and billionaire_question with primary-source figures (Treasury, Census, SEC). Descriptions still call true, sourced stories 'illustrative numbers', which contradicts the 12 Nov rule.

findings.title: Shorts originality ranking (1 Oct 2026) targets re-upload channels
findings.detail: TeamYouTube: 'further prioritize original content and reduce the reach of content re-uploaded from other creators'. Our own stories are not the target; the spam policy's mass-production clause makes variety and sourced facts our defence.

findings.title: Descriptions say 'illustrative numbers' on true stories
findings.detail: Every Short's description uses the same boilerplate line; since 12 Nov every Short is sourced facts. Adopt proposal: name the sources instead (the hard-rule disclaimer stays).

findings.title: US debt $40.58T (Treasury, 10 Nov 2026) is ~$118,700 per American
findings.detail: New top feed topic (score 8.55); reference 1.98M views at 8.3x its channel.

findings.title: Meta: Zuckerberg's salary $1, all other compensation $25.1M in 2025
findings.detail: From the 2026 proxy; new billionaire_question topic.

findings.title: Petrol topic rejected: excise cut in Mar 2026
findings.detail: The 1 Oct 2025 Indian Oil sheet is no longer the latest; no newer official sheet found.
